Two cuts in posterior-mean chronic absence divide twelve schools into up to three grades.

```{=html}

```

## Numerical illustrations {#what-to-try}

- **Tertiles.** States 48 pairs with E = 1.83 and risk .0823 (optimum: 45 pairs, risk .0638).
- **Archived grades.** Cuts 3 and 9 match the archived report (45 pairs, risk .0638).
- **One boundary.** Position 6 gives two grades, 36 pairs, and risk .0913.
- **Higher withholding cost.** At τ = .45, the optimum states 47 pairs at risk .143.

<details>
<summary>Scope and Dashboard notes</summary>

Moving a cut changes both how many comparisons the report states and which schools it compares. The cuts follow the posterior-mean order, while the full search considers every assignment with at most three grades under the same posterior and withholding cost τ. Grade 1 identifies lower chronic absence; schools in the same grade have no stated direction. This twelve-school teaching subset is conditional on a statewide prior fitted to 5,834 eligible schools (prior-estimation uncertainty is not propagated). California's Dashboard colors follow separate status-and-change rules, and the loss comparison provides no measure of school quality, causal effects, or statewide calibration. Related: [Reasons for a withheld comparison](../criteria/why-withheld.qmd) · [The error–disclosure frontier](../grades/frontier.qmd).

</details>

Data: California Department of Education, 2026 California School Dashboard chronic absenteeism data, academic year 2025–26, adapted in postrank 1.1.0 (`pr_case_cde`); <https://www.cde.ca.gov/re/di/cr/index.asp>; not relicensed, provided as is; No CDE endorsement is implied.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true"}
## In postrank

This call uses the supplied posterior to evaluate the fixed tertiles at τ .20.

```r
library(postrank)
g <- pr_case_cde$reference$actions$observed_rate_tertiles
postrank_evaluate(g, pr_case_cde$input, weights = c(negative_chronic_absence = 1), tau = .2)[c("N", "E", "primary_risk")]
```
:::
